reconcile.note: Gill reads Luke's eight days as inclusive of the day of the saying and the day of the transfiguration, while Matthew and Mark count only the days between.

discrepancy.emptyNote: No major public-domain critic presses this as a contradiction — and the leading 19th-c. skeptic, D. F. Strauss, calls the agreement "certainly striking" and reconciles the numbers himself.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: D. F. Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined (1846).

sides.snippet: After six days, Jesus took with him Peter, James, and John his brother, and brought them up into a high mountain by themselves.
sides.verseText: After six days, Jesus took with him Peter, James, and John his brother, and brought them up into a high mountain by themselves.

sides.snippet: It happened about eight days after these sayings, that he took with him Peter, John, and James, and went up onto the mountain to pray.
sides.verseText: It happened about eight days after these sayings, that he took with him Peter, John, and James, and went up onto the mountain to pray.
